improvementsForChallenger: The play surface is a flat mustard poster, not a meadow: add painted value variation, grass tufting, warm/cool patches, and dappled shadows cast from the perimeter trees so the board reads as ground rather than a UI backdrop.

Perimeter vegetation is placeholder-grade: the trees, bushes, and rocks are untextured low-poly blobs in near-uniform dark green with almost no shading gradient or contact shadow into the field (corner-tr and corner-bl are especially empty and unfinished).
The river reads as a glowing neon-cyan ribbon with an outer glow, like a UI path, not water; give it banks, depth, foam, and sun-consistent specular instead of emissive glow.

Commit to a single sun: cards drop crisp shadows to the lower-right but the scenery is lit flat/ambient, so the world and the cards do not share one light; add long warm directional shadows from every tree, rock, and fence post.

The center divider is a perfectly straight flat line with a flat diamond sitting on top of the ground; let its glow fall off onto the grass, add slight organic waver, and let scene shadows interact with it so it exists in the world.
Card fronts are pure flat vector: add subtle paper grain, edge wear, and a lighting response (soft top-light gradient) so the very readable card design also feels like a physical object in the scene.

The ground plane is a flat mustard fill with confetti speckles: there is no grass material, no dappled sun, no hue or value gradient, so the meadow never reads as a lit place; paint an actual grass surface with one light direction.
Trees and bushes are unshaded flat polygon clusters that cast almost no shadows on the ground (corner-tr, corner-br); establish a single sun with consistent cast shadows to ground the scenery.
The cyan river is a glowing UI stroke, not water (corner-tl, corner-br): give it banks, depth color, and lighting that belongs to the scene instead of an outer-glow effect.

Card art is a repeated black-cat silhouette across many distinct cards (Duskfang, Cindermaw, Emberfang, Predator's Mark, Ignite, Last Breath are near-identical); distinct illustrations are required for a shippable board.
Cards sit on the field with small uniform offset shadows and no ground interaction, so they read as pasted stickers; add contact-darkening and shadow softness that responds to the surface.
Unify the palette: teal sleeve edges, purple card backs, and the mustard field clash with no shared color grade or ambient light tying them together.
